subject: General Knowledge
topic: Indian states — facts & firsts — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Pochampally Ikat, a GI-tagged handloom textile woven using a resist-dyeing technique on yarn before weaving, belongs to which Indian state?

options.option_text: Andhra Pradesh (famous for Kalamkari print textiles)
Telangana (Pochampally village, Yadadri Bhongir district)
Odisha (famous for Sambalpuri Ikat weave tradition)
Karnataka (famous for the Ilkal saree heritage craft)

questions.explanation: Pochampally village in Yadadri Bhongir district of Telangana is the birthplace of Pochampally Ikat, a GI-tagged textile. Many candidates answer Andhra Pradesh because Pochampally was part of undivided Andhra Pradesh before the 2014 bifurcation — it now falls entirely in Telangana. Sambalpuri Ikat (Option C) is a distinct Odisha tradition; confusing the two is the second most common error.

questions.stem: As per Census 2011, which Indian state recorded the highest overall literacy rate in the country?

options.option_text: Goa (high literacy, often cited as a near-topper state)
Kerala (achieved over 94% literacy rate, Census 2011 rank 1)
Mizoram (second-highest in NE, close rival to national top)
Tripura (significant literacy gains, strong NE state ranking)

questions.explanation: Kerala recorded 94.0% literacy in Census 2011, topping the national list. Mizoram (91.3%) is the strongest distractor because it ranks very high and is sometimes cited loosely as a topper. Goa (88.7%) is another plausible wrong choice. Tripura is well below these figures. The question tests precision — candidates who know Kerala leads but doubt themselves often flip to Mizoram.

questions.stem: Madhubani painting, also called Mithila art, originates from a district in which Indian state that shares its very name with the painting tradition?

options.option_text: Bihar (Madhubani district, core of Mithila cultural region)
Jharkhand (Hazaribagh district, known for Kohbar wall art)
Uttar Pradesh (Varanasi, centre of Mughal miniature style)
West Bengal (Kalighat tradition, iconic scroll-painting style)

questions.explanation: Madhubani district in Bihar is the geographic and cultural origin of Mithila/Madhubani painting, a GI-tagged folk art depicting themes from Hindu epics using natural pigments. Jharkhand's Hazaribagh Kohbar art is related but distinct; West Bengal's Kalighat painting is a Pat-based scroll tradition that examiners use to trip candidates who know 'folk art of Bengal' but mix up names.

questions.stem: The 'living root bridges', fashioned by training aerial roots of rubber-fig trees across streams over generations, are characteristic of which Indian state?

options.option_text: Arunachal Pradesh (known for bamboo cane suspension bridges)
Assam (Brahmaputra floodplains, known for bamboo-reed walkways)
Meghalaya (Khasi and Jaintia communities, Cherrapunji region)
Manipur (Loktak Lake region, floating phumdi biomass islands)

questions.explanation: Living root bridges are a bio-engineering tradition of the Khasi and Jaintia communities of Meghalaya, especially around Cherrapunji and Mawlynnong. Roots of Ficus elastica are guided across streams and take decades to mature into load-bearing bridges. Arunachal Pradesh uses cane suspension bridges; Manipur's Loktak features floating phumdis — a common distractor because both involve natural materials on water.

questions.stem: India's largest saffron-producing belt, referred to as the 'Saffron Bowl of India', is centred on which town and state?

options.option_text: Himachal Pradesh (Kinnaur district, high-altitude temperate belt)
Uttarakhand (Chamoli district, Himalayan organic farming region)
Jammu & Kashmir (Pampore town, Karewa plateau cultivation zone)
Sikkim (India's first organic state, Eastern Himalayan saffron)

questions.explanation: Pampore town in Pulwama district, J&K, sits on the Karewa (high-plateau) soil that produces the prized GI-tagged Kashmiri saffron. Sikkim is a tempting distractor because its 'organic state' branding is well-publicised, but its saffron output is negligible. Himachal Pradesh (Kinnaur) grows saffron in tiny quantities. The 'Saffron Bowl' tag specifically belongs to Pampore.

questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution grants Nagaland a special provision whereby Parliament can extend a law to the state ONLY with the consent of its Legislative Assembly, protecting Naga customary law?

options.option_text: Article 370 (abrogated in 2019, had applied to Jammu & Kashmir)
Article 371A (exclusive special provision inserted for Nagaland)
Article 371G (analogous special provision that applies to Mizoram)
Article 371C (Hill Areas Committee mechanism applicable to Manipur)

questions.explanation: Article 371A was inserted by the 13th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962, coinciding with Nagaland's statehood. It shields Naga customary law, land ownership, and related practices from Parliamentary override without the state assembly's resolution. Article 371G mirrors this for Mizoram — the most-tested distractor. Article 371C covers Manipur's Hill Areas Committee. Article 370 (now abrogated) was specific to J&K and had a different mechanism entirely.

questions.stem: Tribal areas of which among the following North-East states fall OUTSIDE the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, unlike its neighbours Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram?

options.option_text: Assam (Bodoland TC, Karbi Anglong — active Sixth Schedule ADCs)
Meghalaya (Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills — Sixth Schedule councils)
Manipur (hill tribes governed via Art. 371C Hill Areas Committee)
Mizoram (Chakma, Mara, Lai — Sixth Schedule district councils)

questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2) and 275(1)) covers autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Manipur is the exception — its hill tribal areas are instead managed through the Hill Areas Committee under Article 371C, a separate mechanism. Candidates typically assume all NE states with large tribal populations are under the Sixth Schedule; Manipur's Art. 371C route is the precise fact that hard-tier setters exploit.
